name: OIDC_ISSUER
label: Issuer URL
setupSteps: Enter the base URL of your identity provider's OIDC issuer — the value it publishes as `issuer`, without a trailing slash.
The connector reads {ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration to discover the authorization, token and JWKS endpoints, so no other URLs need configuring.
Keycloak: https://your-host/realms/{realm}. Okta: https://your-org.okta.com. Authentik: https://your-host/application/o/{slug}. ADFS: https://your-host/adfs.
Must be reachable over HTTPS from this deployment, and every endpoint it advertises must share this origin.

name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
label: Client ID
setupSteps: In your identity provider, register a confidential client (one that can hold a secret) for this deployment.
Set its redirect URI to the value below, exactly.
Grant it the `openid` and `email` scopes; the connector requests both regardless and cannot sign anyone in without them.
Ensure the client's ID token includes a verified `email` claim. Sign-in is refused when `email_verified` is not true, because Workshop accounts are keyed by email.

name: OIDC_SCOPES
label: Additional scopes (leave blank unless your provider needs one)
setupSteps: Space-separated scopes to request in addition to `openid` and `email`, which are always included.
Leave blank unless your provider needs an extra scope to release the email claim.
